text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri discuss the latest arrangements for the upcoming Middle East and North Africa Economic Conference. Mubarak will open the conference attended by 63 countries, 850 international companies and 2,000 foreign investors; 188 Egyptian projects worth $33 billion will be put before the conference.
- Mubarak stresses the need to arrive at a balanced and just peace between the Palestinians and Israel.
- U.S. deputy trade secretary says MENA conference is a good opportunity to explore the potential of Egypt's economy.
- Mubarak and Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy meet in Cairo to discuss the requirements for peace. Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says Mubarak stresses the importance of a balanced peace.
- Mubarak to speak on Sunday in front of Parliament.
- Egypt and Namibia square off in Cairo on Friday in World Cup qualifier football match.

- U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher is to visit Cairo next week to attend the economic conference. A U.S. spokesman said that the conference would be an important opportunity for the peace process, because U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross is to accompany Christopher.
- Greek president to visit Cairo next month.
